title: Imagination Is More Important Than Knowledge.
short_teaser: Imagining new possibilities creates the beginning of change.
story: Albert Einstein valued imagination because discoveries often begin before there is proof. Someone first has to imagine what might be possible. Imagining new possibilities creates the beginning of change. Words give shape to ideas that might otherwise remain difficult to hold. A phrase, name, or story can become a doorway into memory, meaning, identity, and a new way of seeing. What makes the moment especially useful is the pattern beneath it: attention came before understanding, and understanding came before change. That pattern is available in everyday life too, whenever we resist the urge to dismiss something simply because it does not yet fit the plan. The lasting importance is simple: every invention begins as an idea.
impact: Every invention begins as an idea. The words we choose can preserve meaning, change perspective, and help an idea travel from one person to another. This matters because the lesson is transferable. It can help someone recognize a pattern, make a more thoughtful choice, or see possibility where they previously saw only a problem.
spark_application: What possibility can you imagine before you know exactly how it will happen? Capture one phrase, word, or sentence that stays with you. Add a note about why it matters and how you might use it. Afterward, save a short note about what you noticed, what surprised you, or what you may want to revisit.
